subject: Indemnity: proposed splits, evidence obligations (MSA + Order Form)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maria Galvez <maria.galvez@lumenix.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Indemnity: proposed splits, evidence obligations (MSA + Order Form)

Hi Maria / team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is our redline (redline_lumenix_msa_v3.docx) and a draft evidence/responsibility matrix (evidence_matrix_lumenix.xlsx) that maps notice windows, evidence owners, and insurance waterfall expectations. High-level positions from Redwood: 

- Defense control: Redwood proposes to retain primary defense control for third-party IP infringement claims that arise from our hosted inference runtime (i.e., model-serving infra and our code). We are open to customer control for claims exclusively arising out of the customer’s own bespoke prompts or content.
- Cap & exclusions: propose a $5M aggregate cap for third-party IP claims tied to the Order Form, except in cases of willful misconduct or proven bad faith where cap is uncapped.
- Insurance: we expect standard commercial general liability + tech E&O limits; Redwood will accept an insurance offset clause (insurer pays first) with a requirement that customer maintain primary coverage.
- Notice & evidence: 30-day initial notice window, 14-day initial acknowledgement, and a clear evidence-preservation checklist (see evidence matrix). Redwood will retain subrogation rights and require cooperation from the customer in discovery.

Can you confirm whether Lumenix needs us to concede defense control for customer-facing user claims, or whether a limited carve-out for customer-controlled claims is acceptable? Also please confirm the procurement timeline — if Lumenix is able to sign the Order Form by the end of next week we can begin dedicated capacity provisioning the week after.

Thanks,

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Legal Operations (contract intake)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline_lumenix_msa_v3.docx (docx), evidence_matrix_lumenix.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Maria Galvez <maria.galvez@lumenix.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Andrew Kline <andrew.kline@bryantlaw.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Indemnity: proposed splits, evidence obligations (MSA + Order Form)

Hannah —

Thanks for the note and the redline. A few high-level reactions from procurement and internal counsel: 

1) Defense control: Lumenix is uncomfortable with Redwood unilaterally controlling the defense for IP claims that impact our customers. If a customer suffers injury (e.g., alleged patent infringement based on model outputs), we need the right to step in and manage the defense or at minimum co-manage.

2) Cap: $5M cap is below expectations for a regulated healthcare SaaS customer with patient impact risks. We need $25M or a higher insurance-backed limit; alternatively a higher cap for IP claims affecting patient workflows.

3) Evidence & timing: We appreciate the matrix. We also need explicit audit evidence (SOC2 report + data retention statements) and a clause that requires Redwood to preserve system logs and sample outputs for 180 days unless otherwise required by law.

I’ve attached Lumenix’s redline notes (lumenix_comments.pdf). Our timeline: procurement wants signed documents before the end of April to align with Q2 spend.

Best,

Maria Galvez
Senior Director, Procurement
Lumenix Therapeutics

Subject: Re: Indemnity: proposed splits, evidence obligations (MSA + Order Form)

Hannah / Ben —

Quick legal read-through and proposed compromise language to present back to Lumenix: 

- Defense control carve: Redwood can retain primary defense control for claims arising from Redwood’s infrastructure, models supplied by Redwood, and our runtime. We will offer a co-control or customer takeover right for claims that are demonstrably caused solely by customer prompts or data (customer bears reasonable burden of proof).
- Cap structure: propose a two-tier cap — $5M for service-related third-party IP claims; $25M aggregate cap where Lumenix can provide justified evidence of heightened regulatory/patient exposure. For willful misconduct or court-ordered damages we propose to keep the cap uncapped.
- Insurance waterfall: require primary insurer for Lumenix with Redwood’s policies contributing where applicable. Add cooperation and subrogation language.
- Logs & retention: we will commit to preserve relevant logs and sample outputs for 180 days for triage, but will require a narrow preservation request (specific time windows and data types) to protect customer data privacy.

Ben — can you confirm commercial appetite for the two-tier cap and whether sales can accept a conditional $25M top tier tied to procurement signoff? I’ll draft specific redline text around defense-control toggles and evidence burden if we have greenlight to move forward.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Team —

Commercial note: Lumenix is a strategic pilot customer for our dedicated capacity roadmap. If procurement is asking for higher cap / customer defense control we should consider conceding on defense control for customer-facing claims only if: 

- Redwood retains subrogation and audit rights;
- Customer must use Redwood-approved panel counsel or agree to Redwood-selected counsel for initial phase;
- There is a 6-month trial with metrics around claim frequency/trigger events and an automatic review at renewal.

If we can secure commitment on a renewal/price-protection clause and a one-time migration discount into Dedicated, I can accept the two-tier cap commercially. Happy to take this to the AMs in EMEA/US to get buy-in.

—Ben

Hannah / Maria / Kimberly / Ben —

We reviewed Redwood’s compromise language and Lumenix is generally comfortable with the two-tier cap and the defense-control carve as described by Kimberly, provided the redline includes: 

1) A narrowly tailored evidence-preservation clause that lists the types of logs (request/response traces, system timestamps, and request-ids) and the preservation process, with specific timelines and a privilege-preserving procedure for shared materials.
2) A clause that requires Redwood to provide SOC2 Type II attestation within 30 days of countersignature and a right to audit once per year, subject to reasonable confidentiality protections.
3) Specific insurance language referencing minimum limits and an instruction that insurers must waive subrogation against the other party where possible.

If Redwood can incorporate the above and send an updated Order Form we are prepared to move to execution. I’ve uploaded a suggested markup to DocuSign: https://docusign.com/txn/ABCD1234 and added comments in HubSpot record HO-98765.

Please let us know when you’ll circulate the follow-up redline.

Best,
Andrew Kline
Partner, Bryant & Kline LLP
Counsel to Lumenix Therapeutics
